anf_compare.notes: No published English was consulted; translated from the PG 70 Greek only.

bible_refs.note: Lemma Καὶ λήψομαι ἐγὼ ἐκ τῶν ἐπιλέκτων τῆς κέδρου ἐκ κορυφῆς = LXX Ezekiel 17:22 (verse continues καρδίας αὐτῶν ἀποκνιῶ, the source of Cyril's 'heart').
The great cedar receiving all into its shade takes up LXX 17:23, where the planted cedar grows great and every bird rests ὑπὸ τὴν σκιὰν αὐτοῦ.
Paraphrase of LXX ὁ ταπεινῶν ξύλον ὑψηλὸν ... ξηραίνων ξύλον χλωρὸν καὶ ἀναθάλλων ξύλον ξηρόν; Cyril uses τεταπείνωκε, ὑγρόν and ἀναβλαστῆναι.

choices.term: ἐν οἷς τὸ ἐπίλεκτον, καὶ οἱονεί τις καρδία γέγονεν ὁ μακάριος Δαβίδ
choices.english: Among them the chosen part, and, as it were, a kind of heart, was the blessed David
choices.why: Both τὸ ἐπίλεκτον and καρδία are predicates of David; splitting them makes 'the chosen' a separate thing.
rejected: Among them is what is chosen, and David became, as it were, a heart

choices.why: Literally 'doing good to him'; said of people toward God, 'serve him well' keeps the sense without suggesting that God needs benefits.
Standard English for the title; 'the God and Father' is a calque.

choices.english: the whole world under the sun
choices.why: ὑφήλιος (sc. γῆ) is 'the land under the sun', the inhabited world.

edition.locus: Frag remainder, early ('It seems, then' to 'by the devil's…')

pass_a_gloss: It seems then to liken to Noah those through faith toward God doing good (εὐεργετοῦντας) to him; to Daniel indeed the wise and clear-sighted (διορατικούς); and Job again those through endurance (ὑπομονῆς), clearly that toward any whatever of the things praised, pleasing him. Lemma: and I will take from the chosen of the cedar from the top [Ezekiel 17:22]. [Cat. f. 208] To cedars he likens, the lofty and most comely, those from Israel, in whom the chosen thing, and as it were some heart (καρδία), became the blessed David, from whom taking, the God and Father planted Emmanuel, who also rose up into a great cedar and received all into his own shade; and knew thereafter the whole land under the sun the power and authority of the all-powerful God. For he has humbled the moist tree, and to grow and sprout again (ἀναβλαστῆναι) he prepared the dry tree, that is, from nations a Church (Ἐκκλησίαν), by the devil's [sentence continues in frag-rem-mid].
pass_b_english: It seems, then, that he likens to Noah those who, through faith in God, serve him well; to Daniel, those who are wise and clear-sighted; and to Job, in turn, those who please him through endurance, clearly meaning endurance in anything at all that is praised.

“And I will take from the chosen parts of the cedar, from its top” (Ezekiel 17:22). He likens to cedars, tall and most beautiful, those who are from Israel. Among them the chosen part, and, as it were, a kind of heart, was the blessed David. From him God the Father took and planted Emmanuel, who also rose up into a great cedar and received all into his own shade (Ezekiel 17:23). And so, from then on, the whole world under the sun came to know the power and authority of God, who can do all things.
For he has brought low the green tree, and has made the dry tree grow and sprout again (Ezekiel 17:24), that is, the Church from among the Gentiles, which by the devil’s…
source_text:
Ἔοικε τοίνυν τῷ μὲν Νῶε παρεικάζειν τοὺς διὰ πίστεως τῆς εἰς Θεὸν
εὐεργετοῦντας αὐτῷ· τῷ γε μὴν ∆ανιὴλ τοὺς σοφούς τε καὶ διορατικούς· Ἰὼβ δὲ
πάλιν τοὺς διά γε τῆς ὑπομονῆς, δῆλον δὲ ὅτι τῆς εἰς πᾶν ὁτιοῦν τῶν ἐπαινουμένων,
εὐαρεστοῦντας αὐτῷ. Καὶ λήψομαι ἐγὼ ἐκ τῶν ἐπιλέκτων τῆς κέδρου ἐκ κορυφῆς.
Cat. f. 208. Κέδροις μὲν ἀπεικάζει ταῖς ὑψηλαῖς καὶ εὐκοσμοτάταις τοὺς ἐξ
Ἰσραὴλ, ἐν οἷς τὸ ἐπίλεκτον, καὶ οἱονεί τις καρδία γέγονεν ὁ μακάριος ∆αβὶδ, ἐξ οὗ
λαβὼν ὁ Θεὸς καὶ Πατὴρ κατεφύτευσε τὸν Ἐμμανουὴλ, ὃς καὶ εἰς κέδρον ἀνέστη
μεγάλην, καὶ εἰσεδέξατο πάντας εἰς ἰδίαν σκιάν· ἔγνω τε λοιπὸν ἡ ὑφήλιος σύμπασα
τὴν τοῦ πάντα ἰσχύοντος Θεοῦ δύναμίν τε καὶ ἐξουσίαν.
Τεταπείνωκε γὰρ τὸ ξύλον τὸ ὑγρὸν, φῦναι δὲ καὶ ἀναβλαστῆναι
παρεσκεύασε τὸ ξύλον τὸ ξηρὸν, τουτέστιν ἐξ ἐθνῶν Ἐκκλησίαν, ταῖς τοῦ διαβόλου
reviewer: claude (Wave A review, clause by clause against the Greek)
review_notes: Replaces a scaffold row that held no translation; the English is new, translated from the locked PG 70 Greek in translations/fe_frag_rem_source.json.
Reviewer fix: τὸ ἐπίλεκτον and καρδία are both said of David; the draft had split them.
Reviewer fix: Ezekiel 17:23 (the shade of the great cedar) cited inline and added to bible_refs.
Reviewer fix: small reorder in the Noah clause so 'him' clearly means God.
Lemma checked against LXX Ezekiel 17:22; the paraphrase checked against Ezekiel 17:23-24.
The section ends mid-sentence at ταῖς τοῦ διαβόλου; frag-rem-mid finishes the clause.
